review_remediation.fifth_review_finding: registry resolution required only that the named id EXIST and that the registry entry assert qualified=true. The properties behind that flag (production/rehearsal verification, capability completeness, exact source binding) were asserted only in validateRegistry(), a separate function. Called on its own, validateEvidenceAgainstRegistry() accepted an artifact that was unverified, capability-incomplete and had no source commit, purely because it claimed qualified=true.
review_remediation.fifth_review_fix: targetQualificationErrors() now holds the target properties in one place and is called from BOTH validateRegistry() and the resolution path, so resolution never depends on a self-asserted flag or on another checker having run first. A rollback target must additionally state how its source_commit was bound, so an asserted binding can never be mistaken for a verified one.

review_remediation.sixth_review_finding: the fifth-review fix removed the dependency on qualified=true but left verification, capability_manifest_covers_required_routes, source_commit and source_commit_binding as self-asserted values. The blocking test — an artifact with a valid-looking dpl_ id, production_verified, capabilities true, 40 hex characters, a declared binding, and zero backing evidence — resolved successfully. The trust boundary had moved, not closed.
review_remediation.sixth_review_fix: qualification is derived: capability completeness is computed against required_capability_routes and every required route must appear in the cited evidence; verification resolves a CURRENT, same-provider evidence entry that names the exact artifact id and carries the required proof stage; source binding resolves evidence connecting that exact artifact id to that exact commit. Cited evidence is hash-verified against the index, so citing tampered evidence fails. 'qualified' is generated and CI asserts it equals the derivation.
review_remediation.sixth_review_consequence: MATERIAL STATUS CHANGE. Applying the derivation to real evidence disqualifies the target this artifact previously named. Rollback moves from 'available for a future deployment' to UNAVAILABLE. The prior availability rested on self-assertion plus a superseded record, not on current evidence.

substring_cooccurrence_qualification.finding: qualification used three independent evidence.text.includes() checks (artifact_id, each required route, source_commit) with nothing binding the hits to one another, so one document describing two deployments could qualify deployment A on deployment B's commit and routes
